title: Submenu
description: A context menu for a track on Abbey Road, with two levels of submenus that read where you are going. Cut diagonally from Add to Playlist toward Seasons and the rows you cross never steal the highlight: the pointer's heading and speed are checked against a safe triangle from where it left the open row to the submenu's near edge, and a short grace timer lets a pause decide. While the triangle is holding the highlight it is drawn over the menu as a hairline wedge, with the cut you made and where your heading meets the submenu, and it fades the moment you land. The menu scales out of the point you clicked, each submenu slides a few pixels from its row on a spring, and one highlight glides between rows, stretching on its leading edge and closing up as it lands. Arrow keys, Enter, Escape and typeahead drive it all with roving focus.
intent: After Linear's submenu safe triangle (https://linear.app/blog/invisible-details) and Ben Kamens' breakdown of Amazon's mega-dropdown aim prediction (https://bjk5.com/post/44698559168/breaking-down-amazons-mega-dropdown): a nested context menu that predicts intent from the pointer's velocity so a diagonal move toward an open submenu never closes it.
